leads.name: Ashland blue ash pair
leads.site: Ashland, the Henry Clay Estate, 120 Sycamore Road
leads.reason: Two blue ash called nearly 300 (estate grounds page), over 300 (director to WEKU 2023) and nearly 400 (another estate page) years old and predating Clay; no source says where on the grounds they stand, no pin; grounds access unclear (tour $25, hours Tue-Sat 10-3:45, grounds-only admission not stated). Needs a location and an access answer from the estate (859-266-8581).

leads.name: Lexington Cemetery cucumbertree magnolia (KY champion)
leads.reason: KY champion listing: circumference 176 in, height 96 ft, crown 74 ft, 'Fayette/Lexington Cemetery'. No location within 170 acres, cannot be told apart on the ground. Cemetery Tree Book PDF (lexcem.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/Lexington-Cemetery-Tree-Book.pdf) is image-only, could not be read here; may give section.

leads.name: Lexington Cemetery American smoketree (KY champion)
leads.reason: KY listing: circumference 110.53 in, height 40 ft, crown 42 ft. Modest tree, no location within the cemetery; search summaries called it national champion (unverified). Lead until the Tree Book gives a section.

leads.name: Ohio buckeye national champion
leads.reason: gatheringgrowth.org: 174 in, 86 ft, crowned 2017, location only 'Lexington, Kentucky'. No site, likely not public (Trees Lexington lists an Ohio buckeye at Catholic Charities, 1310 W Main, a private organisation's grounds, unconfirmed same tree).

leads.name: Duncan Park bur oak
leads.reason: Search result mentions a big bur oak near the entrance; no age, no measurement, no source fetched. Lead.

leads.name: St. Joe's Oak
leads.site: St. Joseph Hospital, with a parking structure built around it
leads.reason: Named in American Forests 'Venerable Trees of the Bluegrass' (2015-10-16); hospital grounds access and location unverified, no age.

leads.name: Floracliff old oaks
leads.reason: 'A Tour of Floracliff's Old Oak Trees' exists but the sanctuary is entry by reservation/event and outside the city; not fetched.

leads.name: UK campus and Arboretum
leads.reason: Nothing old or champion found beyond a state champion red buckeye shrub (13 in); willow oaks planted late 1960s; Trees Lexington tree-of-the-month entries are not ancient. No candidate.
